examples.label: Example 1
examples.code:
Open the confirmation dialog

Try the dialog using its trigger.

methods.name: close(action: "confirm" | "cancel" = "cancel"): void
methods.description: Closes the dialog with action confirm or cancel and emits tp-dialog-close carrying that action; defaults to cancel.
Replaces the title, body nodes and button labels. Supplied nodes are moved into the dialog; omitted title/body become empty and button labels default to Confirm/Cancel.

methods.name: show(): void
methods.description: Opens the internal native dialog in modal mode, blocking interaction with the rest of the page.

events.name: tp-dialog-close
events.description: Emitted when the dialog is closed from one of its actions.

userHelp.introduction: The custom `<tp-dialog>` element displays a confirm/cancel dialog.
userHelp.interactions:
#### Mouse interactions

| Control or gesture | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Using the component | Activate the page's trigger to open the panel. |
| Using the component | Use its controls or links, then close it with the available dismissal control. |

#### Keyboard interactions

| Key or gesture | Result |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Escape</kbd> | Dismiss the panel when its settings allow it. |
| <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>?</kbd> | Open User Help for the component under the pointer, or the focused component if none is hovered. Include <kbd>Shift</kbd> if needed to type <kbd>?</kbd>. |
| <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>?</kbd> | Choose a component from the hierarchy under the pointer, or around the focused component, then open its help. <kbd>Alt</kbd> is <kbd>Option</kbd> on macOS; include <kbd>Shift</kbd> if needed to type <kbd>?</kbd>. |
